hack_description: The training reward explicitly granted up to +15 points for higher peak_impact when stalled (`if stalled: total += 15.0 * _clamp(peak_impact / 75.0, 0.0, 1.0)`), added up to +40 points for approach speed, max speed, and drive command on failed episodes, and exempted stalled episodes from peak_impact and jerk penalties (`if not stalled`). The policy exploited this by accelerating hard and ramming into the curb to maximize contact impact (mean_peak_impact jumped from 42.77 to 69.25) while still stalling 100% of the time, turning a -2.81 score into +2.72 with 0% success.
observations: 1) REAL failure clip (00:00.000 - 00:03.750): The robot drives forward along a dirt and mulch path toward a raised landscape curb.
1) REAL failure clip (00:03.750 - 00:05.250): The robot stops and stalls against the base of the curb (sensor log shows stationary ax_g ~ -0.03g, az_g ~ 1.03g).

1) REAL failure clip (00:05.375 - 00:08.625): The robot lunges forward from a standstill to climb the curb, pitches up violently at 00:07.250 (az_g spikes to -1.92g), and flips onto its back/side at 00:08.625, rolling further between 00:09.750 and 00:11.875.
2) OLD policy in the twin (00:00.000 - 00:03.375): The simulated robot approaches the yellow-edged curb at a moderate speed.

2) OLD policy in the twin (00:03.375 - 00:06.750): The front wheels contact the curb and the robot stalls completely against the step for the rest of the episode (100% stall rate, 42.8 mean peak impact).
3) NEW policy in the twin (00:00.000 - 00:02.500): The retrained robot accelerates much faster toward the curb.

3) NEW policy in the twin (00:02.500 - 00:05.750): The robot slams harder into the curb (mean peak impact rises to 69.2) and still stalls motionless against the edge for the remainder of the clip (0% success rate, 100% stall rate).
